caption: The Lux headlamp exists only while enabled in a compatible Editor world and follows the working camera.
capture_instructions: Draw a lifecycle diagram: Disabled → toolbar click → Enabled/valid editor camera → Create transient point light → camera movement updates position → Disable or world cleanup destroys component. Show map-change recreation as a separate arrow.

caption: Lux separates native UI, input tracking, transient light management and stored preferences into distinct editor classes.
alt: Lux source components and configuration ownership diagram.
capture_instructions: Create a class/data flow diagram including FLuxModule, SLuxViewportControl, FLuxInputProcessor, FLuxViewportTracker, ULuxEditorSubsystem, ULuxProjectSettings, ULuxUserSettings and UPointLightComponent. Indicate ownership and callback direction.

caption: Lux's color and specular settings help isolate material response without editing the material asset.
alt: Material-response comparison under two Lux light settings.
capture_instructions: Capture the same glossy and matte material samples in a perspective viewport under Lux, ideally as a labeled side-by-side comparison with different Specular Scale or Source Radius values. Keep all material properties unchanged.

caption: The inspection light remains a transient editor component while rendering features determine the lighting cost.
alt: Lux editor headlamp features influencing renderer cost.
capture_instructions: Create a conceptual cost diagram showing one Lux point light with attenuation radius, Cast Shadows, volumetric and translucent contributions labeled. Avoid invented frame times or performance numbers.

caption: A single Lux headlamp moves between perspective Level Editor cameras as the user changes the active editing viewport.
alt: Animation transferring Lux tracking between perspective editor viewports.
capture_instructions: Record a two-perspective-viewport Unreal layout with both viewports visible. Click and move camera A, then click and move camera B, showing which view is receiving the tracking light. Use a modest attenuation radius and an overlay label to make the current target unmistakable.

caption: Lux resolves the last interacted perspective Level Editor viewport before using supported fallbacks.
alt: Lux active perspective viewport selection logic.
capture_instructions: Create a decision flow showing a valid tracked SLevelViewport, then matching active Level Editor viewport, then first available perspective fallback. Separate rejected orthographic, PIE and asset-editor clients from valid targets.

caption: Lux's toolbar state, saved preferences and the temporary light are separate concepts.
alt: Lux activation, preferences and transient component comparison.
capture_instructions: Create a three-column annotated still: Lux icon off/on, dropdown settings showing a saved intensity, and the same scene without a placed Light Actor in the Outliner. Keep the purpose of each state distinct.
